pure-vowels.rule: Spanish vowels retain clear qualities without English-style reduction
pure-vowels.example: Do unstressed Spanish vowels normally reduce to English schwa?
pure-vowels.answer: No. Keep a, e, i, o, u clear even when unstressed.

vowel-sound-map.rule: Each of the five vowel letters has a clear basic sound
vowel-sound-map.example: What basic sounds do a, e, i, o and u represent in this lesson's English approximations?
vowel-sound-map.answer: a: ah; e: eh; i: ee; o: oh; u: oo.

silent-h.rule: Written h is silent in the ordinary Spanish words taught here
silent-h.example: What consonant sound does the initial h add in hablar?

j-sound.rule: Spanish j has a back-of-mouth or h-like sound
j-sound.example: Does j in jamón have the English j sound of jam?
j-sound.answer: No. It has a back-of-mouth or h-like sound, varying by region.

hard-c.rule: C before a, o, u has a k sound
hard-c.example: What sound does c represent in casa, unlike c before e or i?

hard-g.rule: G before a, o and u has the hard sound illustrated in gato
hard-g.example: Does g in gato have the same sound as g in gente?
hard-g.answer: No. Gato has hard g before a; gente has the j-like sound before e.

enye-sound.rule: Ñ is a separate letter with a ny-like sound
enye-sound.example: What sound distinguishes ñ in niño from an ordinary n?
enye-sound.answer: A ny-like sound, as in canyon.

trilled-r.rule: Rr and word-initial r use a trill
trilled-r.example: Which r spellings in perro and rosa call for a trill?
trilled-r.answer: The rr in perro and the initial r in rosa.

default-penultimate-stress.rule: Words ending in a vowel, N, or S stress the second-to-last syllable by default
default-penultimate-stress.example: La palabra 'hablan' termina en N, entonces la sílaba acentuada es: ___

default-final-stress.rule: Without a tilde, other final consonants normally indicate final stress
default-final-stress.example: Which syllable is stressed in hablar, written without a tilde?

written-accent.rule: A written stress accent identifies the stressed vowel
written-accent.example: Where does the written accent place stress in médico?

si-accent-contrast.rule: A diacritic accent can distinguish meanings
si-accent-contrast.example: How do sí and si differ in meaning?
si-accent-contrast.answer: Sí means yes; si means if.

tu-accent-contrast.rule: Tú the subject pronoun differs from tu the possessive
tu-accent-contrast.example: How do tú and tu differ in meaning?
tu-accent-contrast.answer: Tú means you; tu means your.

el-accent-contrast.rule: Él the pronoun differs from el the article
el-accent-contrast.example: How do él and el differ in meaning?
el-accent-contrast.answer: Él means he; el means the.

mas-accent-contrast.example: How do más and mas differ, including register?
mas-accent-contrast.answer: Más means more; mas means but and is literary.

seseo-distincion.rule: Seseo and distinción are regional pronunciation systems
seseo-distincion.example: How do Latin American seseo and the distinción common in much of Spain treat z and c before e/i?
seseo-distincion.answer: Seseo gives them an s sound; distinción gives them a th sound distinct from s.

yeismo.rule: Yeísmo merges ll and y, with regional variation in the merged sound
yeismo.example: What happens to the ll/y distinction in yeísmo?
yeismo.answer: Ll and y are pronounced alike.

diaeresis-u.rule: Ü makes u audible in güe and güi
diaeresis-u.example: Why is u pronounced in pingüino but silent in guerra?
diaeresis-u.answer: The diaeresis in güi marks an audible u; plain gue keeps u silent.

soft-g.rule: G before E/I = soft 'H' sound; J is always 'H'-like; H is always silent

definite-agreement.rule: Definite articles match the noun's gender and number

article-specificity.rule: Definite and indefinite articles signal different reference
article-specificity.example: What difference does el libro versus un libro normally signal?
article-specificity.answer: El libro refers to an identifiable book; un libro introduces or refers to an unspecified book.

indefinite-plural.rule: Unos and unas introduce indefinite plural nouns

del-contraction.rule: De plus the article el contracts to del

pronoun-no-contraction.rule: The pronoun él does not trigger article contractions
pronoun-no-contraction.example: Why is Hablo de él not written with del?
pronoun-no-contraction.answer: Él is a personal pronoun, not the article el.

agua-gender.rule: El before a feminine stressed-a noun does not change its gender
agua-gender.example: Does el agua become masculine because it takes el?
agua-gender.answer: No. Agua remains feminine: el agua fría and las aguas frías.

modified-profession.rule: A descriptive modifier can license an indefinite article with a profession

country-articles.rule: Article use with country names varies by name and usage
country-articles.example: Must all country names take an article, and is Perú without el acceptable?
country-articles.answer: No. Most omit it, and both Perú and el Perú are acceptable.

al-contraction.rule: a + el = al, de + el = del (mandatory contractions)

bare-profession.rule: Bare professions after ser normally omit an indefinite article
bare-profession.example: Ella ___ enfermera. (She is a nurse — use the correct form of ser, no article)

legacyAliases.rule: No indefinite article with professions after ser — unless the profession is modified by an adjective
legacyAliases.example: Ella ___ enfermera. (She is a nurse — use the correct form of ser, no article)

gender-tendencies.rule: Noun endings are gender clues, not guarantees
gender-tendencies.example: Does an -a ending guarantee that a Spanish noun is feminine?
gender-tendencies.answer: No. It is a useful tendency, but exceptions such as el día and el mapa must be learned.

feminine-endings.rule: The taught -ción, -sión, -dad and -tad nouns are feminine
feminine-endings.example: What gender do nación, televisión, ciudad and libertad have?
feminine-endings.answer: Feminine: la nación, la televisión, la ciudad, la libertad.

greek-ma.rule: Problema belongs to the masculine Greek-origin -ma group

shortened-nouns.rule: Shortened nouns can keep the gender of their full form
shortened-nouns.example: Why are foto and moto feminine despite ending in -o?
shortened-nouns.answer: They retain the gender of fotografía and motocicleta.

vowel-plural.rule: The unstressed vowel-final nouns taught here add -s

grande-gender.rule: Grande has the same singular form for masculine and feminine nouns

legacyAliases.rule: Adjectives agree in gender and number with their noun; adjectives not ending in -o are invariable for gender
legacyAliases.example: La casa es ___ (big) y los jardines son ___ (beautiful, masc. pl.).

adjective-four-forms.rule: An -o adjective changes for feminine and plural agreement

mixed-group.rule: Conventional agreement uses masculine plural for a mixed-gender group

z-plural.rule: Nouns ending in -z change to -ces in the plural
z-plural.example: Tengo dos ___ en mi mochila. (lápiz, plural)

ar-stem-method.rule: Regular present -ar forms replace the infinitive ending with a person ending
ar-stem-method.example: How do you build a regular present-tense form from hablar?
ar-stem-method.answer: Remove -ar to get habl-, then add the ending for the subject.

ar-third-singular.rule: Él, ella and usted share the -a ending

ar-third-plural.rule: Ellos and ustedes take -an with regular -ar verbs

ar-question.rule: A yes/no question needs no English-style do auxiliary
ar-question.example: Does ¿Hablas inglés? require a Spanish equivalent of do?
ar-question.answer: No. The conjugated verb and question intonation form the question.

ar-negation.rule: No precedes the conjugated verb for ordinary negation

ar-present-ongoing.rule: Spanish present tense covers 'I speak', 'I am speaking', and 'I do speak'

er-ir-differences.rule: Regular -er and -ir present endings differ only for nosotros and vosotros
er-ir-differences.example: Which subjects have different regular present endings in the -er and -ir families?

legacyAliases.rule: -er and -ir verbs share most endings; nosotros differs: -emos (-er) vs -imos (-ir)
legacyAliases.example: Nosotros ___ (beber) agua y ___ (vivir) en la ciudad.

er-ir-third-person.rule: Ellos takes -en in both regular families

er-ir-negation.rule: Negative sentences: place 'no' directly before the conjugated verb

ser-yo.rule: Ser has the irregular yo form soy

ser-profession.rule: A profession identifies what someone is and uses ser

ser-time.rule: Clock time uses ser with singular or plural agreement

estar-location.rule: The physical location of a thing uses estar

estar-progressive.rule: Estar plus a gerund forms the progressive

event-location.rule: The venue where an event takes place uses ser
event-location.example: La fiesta ___ en mi casa. (The party takes place at my house.)

legacyAliases.rule: Ser = identity/origin/profession/time/permanent traits; Estar = location/condition/ongoing action
legacyAliases.example: La fiesta ___ en mi casa. Yo ___ cansado.

listo-contrast.rule: Ser listo and estar listo express different meanings
listo-contrast.example: How does Es lista differ from Está lista?
listo-contrast.answer: Es lista means she is clever; Está lista means she is ready.

rico-contrast.rule: Rico can describe wealth or delicious taste
rico-contrast.example: How does Es rico differ from Está rico in the examples taught here?
rico-contrast.answer: Es rico means he is wealthy; Está rico means it tastes delicious.

malo-contrast.rule: Malo can contrast character with illness
malo-contrast.example: In the table's personal descriptions, how does Es malo differ from Está malo?
malo-contrast.answer: Es malo describes someone as bad or evil; Está malo means he is ill.

bueno-contrast.rule: Bueno can describe moral character or taste
bueno-contrast.example: What meanings do Es bueno and Está bueno illustrate in the table?
bueno-contrast.answer: Es bueno describes a good person; Está bueno describes something that tastes good.

seguro-contrast.rule: Seguro can contrast safety with certainty
seguro-contrast.example: How do Es seguro and Está seguro differ in the table?
seguro-contrast.answer: Es seguro means it is safe; Está seguro means he is certain or sure.

other-adjective-contrasts.rule: Estar vivo expresses life rather than cleverness
other-adjective-contrasts.example: How does Está vivo differ from Es muy vivo?
other-adjective-contrasts.answer: Está vivo means he is alive; Es muy vivo means he is sharp or clever.

aburrido-trait.example: Esa película ___ muy aburrida. (The movie itself is boring as a trait)

permanence-shortcut.rule: Permanence is not a reliable ser-versus-estar test
permanence-shortcut.example: Does a building's permanent physical location require ser rather than estar?
permanence-shortcut.answer: No. Physical location still uses estar.

ir-nosotros.rule: Ir has the irregular nosotros form vamos

ir-future.rule: Ir plus a plus infinitive expresses a future plan

tener-stem.rule: Tener changes e to ie in tú, él and ellos present forms

tener-nosotros.rule: Nosotros retains the unchanged stem in tener

tener-obligation.rule: Tener que plus infinitive expresses obligation

hacer-yo.rule: Hacer has the irregular yo form hago

salir-yo.rule: Salir has an irregular yo form in the present indicative

legacyAliases.rule: Many verbs are irregular ONLY in yo: salgo, pongo, traigo, hago, conozco, doy, sé
legacyAliases.example: Yo ___ (salir) a las ocho y ___ (poner) la música.

poner-yo.rule: Poner has the present yo form pongo

saber-yo.rule: Saber has the accented present yo form sé

traer-yo.rule: Traer has the irregular present yo form traigo

conocer-yo.rule: Conocer has the present yo form conozco

dar-yo.rule: Dar has the present yo form doy

decir-yo.rule: Decir combines an irregular yo form with stem-changing present forms

venir-tu.rule: Venir changes e to ie with tú

plan-versus-obligation.rule: Ir a and tener que distinguish plans from obligation
plan-versus-obligation.example: How does Voy a estudiar differ from Tengo que estudiar?
plan-versus-obligation.answer: Voy a estudiar means I am going to study; Tengo que estudiar means I have to study.

legacyAliases.rule: Ir + a + infinitive = future plans ('going to'); Tener + que + infinitive = obligation ('have to')
legacyAliases.example: Mañana ___ (ir) a visitar a mi abuela y ___ (tener) que comprar flores.

del-contraction.rule: De plus the article el contracts to del

no-pronoun-contraction.rule: Contractions apply to el the article, not él the pronoun
no-pronoun-contraction.example: Why do we write Hablo de él rather than Hablo del?
no-pronoun-contraction.answer: Él means him and is a pronoun, not the article el.

feminine-no-contraction.rule: A plus la does not contract

personal-a.rule: Personal 'a' is required before specific people (and pets) as direct objects
personal-a.example: Llamo ___ mi hermana todos los días.

personal-a-scope.rule: Personal a distinguishes identified people from ordinary things or nonspecific searches
personal-a-scope.example: Why does Veo a María use a, while Busco un médico can omit it?
personal-a-scope.answer: María is identified; un médico can mean any doctor, not a particular person.

destination-a.rule: A marks a destination after ir

material-de.rule: De introduces material in the illustrated noun phrase

transport-en.rule: En introduces the illustrated means of transport

por-para-preview.rule: English for does not uniquely determine por or para
por-para-preview.example: Why do Gracias por tu ayuda and Esto es para ti use different words for for?
por-para-preview.answer: Por introduces the reason for thanks; para identifies the intended recipient.

al-contraction.rule: a + el = al (mandatory contraction); a + la stays separate — never contracts

pro-drop.example: Why can Hablo español omit yo?
pro-drop.answer: The verb form and context identify the speaker, so the subject pronoun is unnecessary.

pronoun-emphasis.rule: Explicit subject pronouns can mark contrast
pronoun-emphasis.example: What does keeping yo and tú add in Yo trabajo, tú no?
pronoun-emphasis.answer: It contrasts who works: I do, but you do not.

usted-regional-register.rule: Usted does not express social distance in every community
usted-regional-register.example: Does usted always mean the speaker is being distant or formal?
usted-regional-register.answer: No. In some communities, including many Colombian contexts, it is also used warmly with intimates.

voseo.rule: The River Plate vos form of tener is tenés

ustedes-latin-america.rule: In Latin America, 'ustedes' covers ALL plural 'you' — formal and informal
ustedes-latin-america.example: ¿Cómo están ___? (asking a group of friends in Mexico City)

vosotros-spain.rule: Much of Spain distinguishes informal vosotros from formal ustedes
vosotros-spain.example: Which plural address form is commonly informal in much of Spain, unlike everyday Latin American usage?

usted-agreement.rule: Usted takes third-person singular verb agreement

ambiguous-subject.rule: Shared verb forms may need an explicit subject for clarity
ambiguous-subject.example: Can trabaja alone distinguish él, ella and usted without context?
ambiguous-subject.answer: No. They share the same verb form; context or an explicit pronoun clarifies the subject.

nosotras.rule: An all-female group uses nosotras in the traditional pronoun system

question-punctuation.rule: Written direct questions use both question marks
question-punctuation.example: Punctuate the direct question Dónde vives.

cual-identification.rule: 'Qué' asks for definitions; 'cuál/cuáles' asks to choose from options
cual-identification.example: ¿___ es tu número de teléfono? (asking someone to report their specific number)

que-definition.rule: Qué es asks for a definition
que-definition.example: ¿___ es un taco? (asking what a taco is)

porque-answer.rule: Porque introduces a reason rather than asking why

porque-noun.rule: El porqué is a noun meaning the reason
porque-noun.example: What role does porqué have in No entiendo el porqué?
porque-noun.answer: It is a noun meaning the reason or the why.

por-que-relative.rule: Unaccented por que can be a preposition plus a relative pronoun
por-que-relative.example: What is por que doing in La razón por que llegué tarde?
por-que-relative.answer: It combines the preposition por with relative que, meaning for which.

cuanto-agreement.rule: Interrogative cuánto agrees with the noun it modifies
cuanto-agreement.example: ¿___ agua queda? (How much water is left?)

quienes-plural.rule: Quién becomes quiénes for a plural identity question

interrogative-accent.rule: All Spanish question words carry a written accent mark (tilde)

direct-object.rule: A feminine singular direct object is replaced by la

direct-indirect-contrast.rule: Direct and indirect objects have different roles
direct-indirect-contrast.example: In Le doy el libro a Ana, which expression is the thing given and which identifies the recipient?
direct-indirect-contrast.answer: El libro is the direct object; le and a Ana identify the indirect-object recipient.

io-plural.rule: Les refers to plural third-person recipients
io-plural.example: ___ cuento una historia a los niños.

infinitive-attachment.rule: Object pronouns may attach to an infinitive in a verbal phrase
infinitive-attachment.example: ¿Puedes ___? (give it to me — IO me + DO lo, attached to dar)

legacyAliases.rule: Object pronouns attach to infinitives, gerunds, and affirmative imperatives — or go before the conjugated verb
legacyAliases.example: ¿Puedes ___ el libro? (give it to me — IO me + DO lo, attached to the infinitive dar)

finite-placement.rule: Object pronouns normally precede an ordinary finite verb
finite-placement.example: ___ veo. (I see him; general direct-object pattern)

gerund-placement.rule: A progressive permits pronouns before estar or attached to the gerund
gerund-placement.example: Rewrite Estoy llamándote with te before the conjugated verb.

command-attachment.rule: Affirmative commands require attached object pronouns
command-attachment.example: In an affirmative command meaning Give it to me, can me lo stand before the command verb?

io-before-do.example: ___ mando. (I send it to you; la carta, tú)

le-to-se.rule: le/les become 'se' before lo/la/los/las — the sequence le+lo is forbidden
le-to-se.example: ¿Le diste las llaves a Juan? Sí, ___ ___ di. (IO + DO)

se-clarification.rule: The replacement se does not identify the recipient's number or gender
se-clarification.example: How does a ella help in Se lo doy a ella?
se-clarification.answer: It identifies her as the recipient, since se alone is ambiguous.

leismo-scope.rule: Accepted male-person singular leísmo is a limited regional alternative
leismo-scope.example: Does accepted Le vi for I saw him license le for every direct object?
leismo-scope.answer: No. The accepted alternative concerns a singular male person; it is not a general replacement for lo/la/los/las.

mi-accent.rule: Possessive mi and prepositional mí differ
mi-accent.example: How do mi in mi casa and mí in para mí differ?
mi-accent.answer: Mi means my and has no accent; mí means me after a preposition and has an accent.

long-possessive-position.rule: A stressed possessive follows the noun

standalone-article.rule: A possessive replacing a known noun can take its definite article
standalone-article.example: Mi libro es azul; ___ es rojo. (yours; el libro)

predicate-no-article.rule: Predicative possession after ser normally omits the article

possessed-agreement.rule: Possessives agree with the THING owned in gender and number — not with the owner
possessed-agreement.example: Tenemos ___ maletas listas para el viaje. (our — fem. pl.)

su-ambiguity.rule: Su does not uniquely identify its owner
su-ambiguity.example: Does su carro alone tell you whether the car is his, hers, yours or theirs?
su-ambiguity.answer: No. Context identifies the owner; de él, de ella, de usted or de ellos can clarify.

su-clarification.rule: De plus a pronoun can make the owner explicit
su-clarification.example: Rewrite su casa to unambiguously mean her house.

mi-number.rule: Short possessives mi/tu/su never change for gender — only for number (mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus)

legacyAliases.rule: Short possessives mi/tu/su never change for gender — only for number (mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus)
legacyAliases.example: Perdí ___ llaves y ___ cartera. (my keys, my wallet — both belong to me)

distance-tiers.rule: Este, ese and aquel express three introductory distance tiers
distance-tiers.example: What distances do este, ese and aquel represent in the basic three-tier model?
distance-tiers.answer: Este is near the speaker; ese is near the listener; aquel is far from both.

distant-feminine.rule: Distant feminine plural nouns take aquellas
distant-feminine.example: ___ montañas están lejos de los dos. (those mountains over there)

neuter-situation.rule: Neuter forms (esto/eso/aquello) refer to unidentified things or whole situations — they never modify a specific noun
neuter-situation.example: No entiendo ___. (referring to the whole situation — near-neutral distance)

neuter-limits.rule: Neuter demonstratives have no plural and cannot modify nouns
neuter-limits.example: Can esto be pluralized or placed before libro as its determiner?
neuter-limits.answer: No. Neuter demonstratives stand alone and have no plural; use este libro or estos libros.

temporal-distance.rule: Aquel can express a remote time as well as a remote place
temporal-distance.example: What kind of distance does aquellos tiempos express?
temporal-distance.answer: Temporal distance: those remote or nostalgically remembered times.

demonstrative-accent.rule: Current optional demonstrative accents are limited to potentially ambiguous pronoun uses
demonstrative-accent.example: Is éste an unrestricted alternative for every pronoun use of este under current RAE guidance?
demonstrative-accent.answer: No. An optional tilde is limited to pronominal uses with a risk of ambiguity; writing este without it is recommended.

near-plural-agreement.rule: Demonstratives agree in gender and number with the noun; use neuter forms (esto/eso/aquello) for vague references
near-plural-agreement.example: ___ estudiantes son de México. (these students — mixed group, plural)

ar-preterite-nosotros.rule: Regular -ar nosotros forms overlap in present and preterite
ar-preterite-nosotros.example: Does hablamos alone distinguish we speak from we spoke?
ar-preterite-nosotros.answer: No. The form is identical; context identifies the tense.

ar-preterite-third.rule: Regular -ar preterite él forms end in -ó
ar-preterite-third.example: Ayer ella ___ con Ana. (hablar; completed conversation)

er-ir-preterite.rule: Regular -er and -ir verbs share preterite endings

bounded-not-once.rule: Bounded aspect matters more than a trigger word or a single occurrence
bounded-not-once.example: Can the indefinido describe three visits within a finished week, rather than only one event?
bounded-not-once.answer: Yes. Repeated actions can be presented as a completed, bounded whole.

hacer-third.rule: Hacer has the irregular unaccented preterite hizo with él

irregular-stem-tener.rule: Tener uses tuv- in the preterite
irregular-stem-tener.example: Ayer yo ___ mucho trabajo. (tener; bounded past situation)

irregular-estar.rule: Estar uses estuv- in the preterite
irregular-estar.example: Ayer él ___ aquí dos horas. (estar; bounded stay)

irregular-poder.rule: Poder uses pud- in the preterite
irregular-poder.example: Finalmente yo ___ abrir la puerta. (poder; preterite)

irregular-poner.rule: Poner uses pus- in the preterite
irregular-poner.example: Yo ___ el libro en la mesa. (poner; preterite)

irregular-saber.rule: Saber uses sup- in the preterite
irregular-saber.example: Ayer yo ___ la verdad. (saber; found out)

irregular-querer.rule: Querer uses quis- in the preterite

irregular-venir.rule: Venir uses vin- in the preterite

irregular-traer.rule: Traer uses traj- and plural -eron in the preterite

j-stem-plural.rule: Preterite j stems take -eron rather than -ieron

strong-stem-accents.rule: The taught strong preterite stems use unaccented endings
strong-stem-accents.example: Do tuve, estuvo and pusieron take the written accents of regular hablé or comió?
strong-stem-accents.answer: No. These irregular strong-stem forms use unaccented endings.

dar-ver-accents.rule: The short preterite forms di and vi have no written accent
dar-ver-accents.example: Write the yo preterite of ver with correct accentuation.

ser-ir-preterite.rule: The preterite of 'ser' and 'ir' are identical: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron
ser-ir-preterite.example: Ayer ___ al mercado con mi mamá. (went — ir)

car-spelling.rule: Preterite yo forms of -car verbs use qu before é

gar-spelling.rule: Preterite yo forms of -gar verbs use gu before é

zar-spelling.rule: Preterite yo forms of -zar verbs use c before é

ar-preterite-yo.rule: Preterite trigger words: ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, el año pasado, hace X días, en [year]
ar-preterite-yo.example: La semana pasada ___ con mis amigos. (I spoke — hablar, yo)

ar-imperfect-nosotros.example: Nosotros ___ español cada día. (hablar; past habit)

er-ir-imperfect.rule: Regular -er and -ir imperfects share accented -ía endings

shared-imperfect-form.rule: Yo and él/ella/usted share imperfect forms
shared-imperfect-form.example: Does hablaba alone distinguish I used to speak from she used to speak?
shared-imperfect-form.answer: No. Context or an explicit subject is needed.

ser-imperfect.rule: Ser has the irregular imperfect era

ver-imperfect.rule: Ver retains ve- before its imperfect ending

past-habit.rule: Use the imperfecto for habits, descriptions, and background states in the past
past-habit.example: Cuando era niño, ___ al fútbol todos los días. (jugar, él)

past-age.rule: Background age in the past uses imperfect tener

past-clock-time.rule: Background clock time uses imperfect ser
past-clock-time.example: ___ las tres cuando llamó. (It was three.)

polite-imperfect.rule: The imperfect can soften a present request
polite-imperfect.example: Must Quería un café, por favor mean that the speaker no longer wants coffee?
polite-imperfect.answer: No. It can be a polite present request: I would like a coffee, please.

ir-imperfect.rule: Only three imperfect irregulars: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía)
ir-imperfect.example: Cuando tenía diez años, ___ a ver a mi abuela todos los domingos. (ir, yo)

legacyAliases.rule: Only three imperfect irregulars: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía)
legacyAliases.example: Cuando tenía diez años, ___ a mi abuela todos los domingos. (ir, yo)

aspect-over-triggers.rule: A time expression is a guide rather than a mechanical tense rule
aspect-over-triggers.example: Does ayer force the indefinido for every verb in a sentence?
aspect-over-triggers.answer: No. The speaker's completed-versus-ongoing viewpoint still determines aspect.

bounded-duration.rule: A long action can be presented as a completed whole
bounded-duration.example: Why can Vivió en Madrid tres años use the indefinido despite lasting three years?
bounded-duration.answer: The residence is presented as a bounded, completed period.

canvas-mnemonic.rule: The canvas and brushstroke image maps background to event
canvas-mnemonic.example: In the canvas-and-brushstroke memory aid, which tense supplies each part?
canvas-mnemonic.answer: The imperfecto is the canvas of background; the indefinido is the brushstroke of the completed event.

snapshot-film-mnemonic.rule: Snapshot versus film is a viewpoint mnemonic
snapshot-film-mnemonic.example: What do snapshot and film playing stand for in this lesson's past-tense memory aid?
snapshot-film-mnemonic.answer: Snapshot represents a completed whole in the indefinido; film playing represents ongoing or repeated background in the imperfecto.

aspect-definition.rule: Perfective and imperfective describe viewpoints on an event
aspect-definition.example: What contrast does Leí el libro versus Leía el libro express?
aspect-definition.answer: Leí presents the reading as a completed whole; leía presents it as in progress or habitual without asserting completion.

saber-aspect.rule: Saber can contrast finding out with an ongoing state of knowledge
saber-aspect.example: How do Supe la verdad ayer and Sabía la verdad todo el tiempo differ?
saber-aspect.answer: Supe means I found out at that point; sabía describes already knowing over time.

conocer-aspect.rule: Conocer can contrast first meeting with ongoing acquaintance
conocer-aspect.example: What common contrast do conocí a Ana and conocía a Ana express?
conocer-aspect.answer: Conocí a Ana can mean I met Ana; conocía a Ana means I knew or was acquainted with Ana.

poder-aspect.rule: Completed poder can express achieving a result
poder-aspect.example: What common contrast do pude and podía express in a completed success versus a background ability?
poder-aspect.answer: Pude can mean I managed to; podía describes I could or was able to as a background ability.

querer-aspect.rule: Querer can gain an attempt reading in a completed event
querer-aspect.example: In the readings taught here, how can quise differ from quería?
querer-aspect.answer: Quise can mean I tried to; quería describes an ongoing wish, I wanted to.

background-reading.rule: Indefinido = completed event; Imperfecto = background, habit, or ongoing state
background-reading.example: Mientras ___ (leer, yo), mi perro entró. (reading already in progress)

legacyAliases.rule: Indefinido = completed event; Imperfecto = background, habit, or ongoing state
legacyAliases.example: Mientras ___ (leer, yo), mi perro ___ (entrar, preterite). Fill both blanks.

foreground-event.rule: A completed event can interrupt imperfect background
foreground-event.example: Mientras leía, mi perro ___. (entrar; completed entrance)

reflexive-meaning.rule: A reflexive pronoun refers back to the subject
reflexive-meaning.example: Who is being washed in María se lava?

reflexive-nosotros.rule: Nos is the reflexive pronoun for nosotros

reflexive-infinitive.rule: A reflexive pronoun can attach to an infinitive in a verbal phrase
reflexive-infinitive.example: Rewrite Me quiero lavar with the pronoun attached to the infinitive.

reflexive-gerund.rule: Gerund attachment preserves the original stress with a tilde
reflexive-gerund.example: Estoy ___. (ducharse, yo; attach the pronoun to the gerund)

reflexive-command-contrast.rule: Affirmative and negative commands place reflexive pronouns differently
reflexive-command-contrast.example: How is te placed in the tú commands Wash yourself and Do not wash yourself?
reflexive-command-contrast.answer: Attached in Lávate; before the verb in No te laves.

lavarse-yo.rule: Reflexive infinitives end in -se; conjugate the stem verb and match the pronoun to the subject
lavarse-yo.example: Yo ___ los dientes todas las mañanas. (lavarse)

pronominal-not-literal.rule: A pronominal verb need not express literal self-directed action
pronominal-not-literal.example: Does irse mean to go oneself in a literal reflexive sense?
pronominal-not-literal.answer: No. It means to leave or go away.

dormirse-onset.rule: 'Dormirse' = to fall asleep (onset); 'dormir' = to sleep (ongoing state)
dormirse-onset.example: El niño ___ enseguida después de la cena. (dormirse, preterite, él)

regular-tu-command.rule: Regular affirmative tú commands match the third-person singular present indicative

formal-command.rule: Usted commands use present subjunctive forms
formal-command.example: ___ con el médico. (hablar; affirmative usted command)

plural-command.rule: Ustedes commands use plural present subjunctive forms

vosotros-command.rule: A regular affirmative vosotros command replaces infinitive r with d
vosotros-command.example: ___ más despacio. (hablar; affirmative vosotros command, Spain)

negative-tu-command.rule: Negative tú commands use present subjunctive rather than affirmative imperative forms

irregular-command-mnemonic.rule: The eight-beat command mnemonic maps short forms to their infinitives
irregular-command-mnemonic.example: Recall Di-Haz-Ve-Ven / Ten-Pon-Sal-Sé and map each beat to its infinitive.
irregular-command-mnemonic.answer: Di → decir; haz → hacer; ve → ir; ven → venir; ten → tener; pon → poner; sal → salir; sé → ser.

decir-command.rule: 8 irregular affirmative tú commands: di, haz, ve, ven, ten, pon, sal, sé
decir-command.example: ___ la verdad siempre. (decir, tú — affirmative command)

command-pronoun-position.rule: Pronouns attach in affirmative commands and precede the verb in negative commands
command-pronoun-position.example: How does pronoun placement differ in Dámelo and No me lo des?
command-pronoun-position.answer: The affirmative attaches me lo; the negative places me lo before the verb.

attached-command-accent.rule: Attached command pronouns can require a stress-preserving tilde
attached-command-accent.example: Attach lo to the affirmative tú command compra, preserving its stress.

salir-negative-command.rule: Negative commands always use the present subjunctive; object pronouns go before the verb
salir-negative-command.example: No ___ (salir, tú, negative command) sin permiso.

number-linking.rule: Compound tens use y, unlike the fused forms from 16 to 29

hundreds-agreement.rule: Hundreds from two hundred agree with the noun's gender

cien-exact.rule: 'Cien' before a noun or alone; 'ciento' when followed by more digits (101-199)

ciento-compound.rule: One hundred followed by tens or units uses ciento

mil-invariable.rule: Mil stays singular in cardinal multiples

million-de.rule: Millón and millones take de directly before a noun

ordinal-shortening.rule: Primero shortens to primer before a masculine singular noun

weekday-frequency.rule: The article distinguishes a specific weekday from a weekly habit
weekday-frequency.example: How do el lunes and los lunes differ?
weekday-frequency.answer: El lunes means on a specific Monday; los lunes means on Mondays habitually.

date-structure.rule: Dates put the day before de plus the lowercase month
date-structure.example: Write March 5 as a Spanish date phrase.

first-day-date.rule: The first day permits primero as well as uno
first-day-date.example: Is el primero de enero incorrect because Spanish dates normally use cardinal numbers?
first-day-date.answer: No. Primero is common for the first day, especially in Latin America; uno is also used.

time-one.rule: One o'clock takes singular es la

time-quarter-to.rule: Menos cuarto subtracts a quarter hour from the following hour
time-quarter-to.example: What time is Son las cinco menos cuarto?

time-at.rule: A la or a las introduces the time at which something happens

time-plural.rule: 'Es la una' (singular) but 'Son las dos/tres/...' (plural) for all other hours
time-plural.example: — ¿Qué hora es? — ___ las ocho y media.

unequal-comparison.rule: Unequal adjective comparisons use más or menos plus que

numeric-threshold.rule: A numeric threshold after más uses de
numeric-threshold.example: Hay más ___ cien personas. (over one hundred)

equal-adjective.rule: Equality with an adjective or adverb uses tan plus como

equal-noun.rule: Tanto agrees with a noun in equality comparisons

tan-tanto-contrast.rule: Tan modifies adjectives or adverbs; tanto modifies nouns
tan-tanto-contrast.example: What determines tan versus tanto in comparisons of equality?
tan-tanto-contrast.answer: Use tan with an adjective or adverb; use tanto/a/os/as with a noun, agreeing with that noun.

age-size-contrast.rule: Age comparisons and physical size comparisons need not use the same form
age-size-contrast.example: Must a physically bigger dog be described with mayor rather than más grande?
age-size-contrast.answer: No. Más grande is natural for physical size; mayor commonly expresses greater age or rank.

better-comparison.rule: 'Mejor' and 'peor' replace 'más bueno' and 'más malo' for quality comparisons
better-comparison.example: Esta película es ___ que la anterior. (better)

relative-superlative.rule: Relative superlatives identify the extreme member of a comparison set
relative-superlative.example: Es ___ alta de la clase. (the tallest; she)

superlative-set.rule: De introduces the comparison set in the taught superlative pattern

absolute-versus-relative.rule: An absolute superlative intensifies without identifying a winner in a set
absolute-versus-relative.example: How does altísimo differ from el más alto de la clase?
absolute-versus-relative.answer: Altísimo means extremely tall; el más alto de la clase means the tallest in the class.

superlative-spelling-c.rule: Rico changes c to qu before -ísimo

superlative-spelling-g.rule: Largo changes g to gu before -ísimo

absolute-facil.rule: Absolute superlative: drop final vowel + add -ísimo/-ísima; watch spelling changes (c→qu, g→gu)
absolute-facil.example: Este examen es ___. (absolute superlative of fácil — extremely easy)

planned-future.rule: A planned future can use present ir + a + infinitive

future-nosotros.rule: Nosotros adds -emos to the full infinitive in the future

future-vosotros.rule: Vosotros uses infinitive + -éis in the future
future-vosotros.example: Vosotros ___ mañana. (hablar, future; informal plural in much of Spain)

future-irregular-stems.rule: Irregular future stems keep regular endings and recur in the conditional
future-irregular-stems.example: Do the shortened future stems also need a separate set of person endings?
future-irregular-stems.answer: No. Use the regular future endings; the same irregular stems also recur in the conditional.

future-tener.rule: Tener uses tendr- in the future

future-hacer.rule: Hacer uses har- in the future

future-poder.rule: Poder uses podr- in the future

future-decir.rule: Decir uses dir- in the future

future-querer.rule: Querer uses querr- in the future

future-saber.rule: Saber uses sabr- in the future

future-venir.rule: Venir uses vendr- in the future

future-salir.rule: Salir uses saldr- in the future

future-poner.rule: Poner uses pondr- in the future

future-haber.rule: Existential haber uses singular habrá in the future
future-haber.example: En 2050 ___ más robots. (haber, future: there will be)

future-caber.rule: Caber uses cabr- in the future

future-valer.rule: Valer uses valdr- in the future

present-conjecture.rule: Futuro simple expresses conjecture about the present (must be / probably)
present-conjecture.example: No sé qué hora es. ___ las nueve. (must be)

future-choice.rule: Future choices reflect context and register, not a strict near/far time boundary
future-choice.example: Is ir a restricted to near events, with futuro simple obligatory for distant events?
future-choice.answer: No. These are tendencies: ir a is common for conversational plans, while futuro simple often suits predictions, formal writing and present conjecture.

conditional-regular.rule: Regular conditional endings attach to the full infinitive

conditional-endings.rule: All six conditional endings contain accented í
conditional-endings.example: Give the conditional endings in yo, tú, él, nosotros, vosotros, ellos order.

conditional-irregular.rule: Conditional uses the same irregular stems as the future tense (tendr-, har-, podr-, dir-, querr-...)
conditional-irregular.example: Con más tiempo, ___ (poder, yo) estudiar más.

hypothetical-result.rule: An unreal present/future condition commonly pairs imperfect subjunctive with conditional result

polite-request.rule: The conditional can soften a request

past-conjecture.rule: The conditional can express a conjecture about a past situation
past-conjecture.example: In a guess about a past scene, does Serían las diez describe a definite future appointment?
past-conjecture.answer: No. It means it must have been about ten o'clock.

reported-future.rule: Future-in-the-past: use conditional when a past verb reports a future event
reported-future.example: Ella prometió que ___ (venir) a la fiesta.

si-condition.rule: Hypothetical conditional si takes imperfect subjunctive, not conditional
si-condition.example: Si yo ___ tiempo, iría. (tener; hypothetical condition)

opposite-vowels.rule: Regular present subjunctives use the present yo stem with opposite-vowel endings
opposite-vowels.example: After dropping -o from the present yo form, which vowel series do -ar verbs and -er/-ir verbs use?
opposite-vowels.answer: -ar uses e endings; -er and -ir use a endings.

ar-subjunctive.rule: Tú present subjunctive of regular -ar verbs ends in -es

yo-irregular-transfer.rule: A yo stem such as teng- carries into the present subjunctive

conocer-transfer.rule: Conozco supplies conozc- for the present subjunctive

irregular-estar.rule: Estar has accented esté in singular yo/él present subjunctive

legacyAliases.rule: The 6+1 fully irregular present subjunctives: sea, esté, vaya, haya, dé, sepa, vea
legacyAliases.example: Espero que todo ___ (estar) bien.

irregular-ser.rule: Ser has sea in the present subjunctive

irregular-ir.rule: Ir uses vay- in the present subjunctive

irregular-haber.rule: Existential haber uses haya in present subjunctive

irregular-dar.rule: Dar has accented dé in yo/él present subjunctive

irregular-saber.rule: Saber uses sep- in present subjunctive

irregular-mnemonic.rule: DIS HES recalls six irregular present-subjunctive verbs
irregular-mnemonic.example: Expand the DIS HES mnemonic into its six infinitives.
irregular-mnemonic.answer: Dar, Ir, Saber, Haber, Estar, Ser.

weirdo-mnemonic.rule: WEIRDO groups common subjunctive contexts rather than replacing construction-specific rules
weirdo-mnemonic.example: What do the six WEIRDO letters stand for in this lesson?
weirdo-mnemonic.answer: Wishes, Emotion, Impersonal expressions, Recommendations, Doubt/Denial, Ojalá.

same-subject-wish.rule: A simple same-subject wish normally takes an infinitive

impersonal-subjunctive.rule: Es importante que takes subjunctive in the taught recommendation
impersonal-subjunctive.example: Es importante que tú ___ a tiempo. (llegar)

uncertainty-not-enough.rule: Mood depends on the construction, not uncertainty alone
uncertainty-not-enough.example: Why does No sé si viene use indicative even though the speaker is uncertain?
uncertainty-not-enough.answer: An indirect question with si does not automatically trigger subjunctive; compare Dudo que venga.

ojala-subjunctive.rule: Ojalá introduces a wish with subjunctive, with or without que

legacyAliases.rule: Subjunctive is triggered in que-clauses after WEIRDO expressions (Wish, Emotion, Impersonal, Recommendation, Doubt, Ojalá)
legacyAliases.example: ___ que haya paz en el mundo. (Ojalá)

preterite-base.rule: Build the imperfect subjunctive from third-person plural preterite minus -ron
preterite-base.example: Which indicative form supplies the imperfect-subjunctive stem, and what do you remove?

irregular-decir-base.rule: Dijeron supplies dije- for imperfect subjunctive
irregular-decir-base.example: Quería que yo te lo ___. (decir, -ra form)

two-series-scope.rule: The -ra/-se alternatives overlap in ordinary subjunctive clauses, not every use
two-series-scope.example: Can -ra and -se be exchanged in an ordinary si-condition, and does that mean every use is interchangeable?
two-series-scope.answer: They can alternate in ordinary subjunctive si-conditions, but not freely in uses such as polite quisiera.

nosotros-accent.rule: Nosotros imperfect subjunctive carries a written accent

se-series.rule: The -se series uses the same preterite-derived base

hypothetical-condition.rule: Hypothetical si-clauses: si + imperfect subjunctive → conditional result
hypothetical-condition.example: Si ___ (tener, yo) más tiempo, aprendería más idiomas.

real-condition.rule: Open real conditions use indicative rather than hypothetical imperfect subjunctive
real-condition.example: How does Si tengo tiempo, voy differ from Si tuviera tiempo, iría?
real-condition.answer: The first presents an open real possibility; the second presents a hypothetical or remote condition.

past-trigger.rule: A past wish commonly takes imperfect subjunctive in a past viewpoint
past-trigger.example: Quería que tú ___. (venir, -ra form; past viewpoint)

polite-quisiera.rule: 'Quisiera' (imperfect subjunctive of querer) = I would like — ultra-polite alternative to 'querría'
polite-quisiera.example: ___ un café con leche, por favor.

por-cause.rule: Por introduces a reason for thanks

por-exchange.rule: Por marks what is exchanged or paid for

duration-variation.rule: Por can mark duration, but is not mandatory across varieties
duration-variation.example: Must a duration such as dos horas always be introduced by por?
duration-variation.answer: No. Por is possible, especially in some American varieties; a bare duration or durante is also common.

por-agent.rule: Por introduces the agent of the taught passive

por-route.rule: Por marks a route through or along a place

por-rate.rule: Por expresses a rate or frequency per unit

legacyAliases.rule: Por = cause/exchange/duration/through; Para = purpose/destination/deadline/recipient
legacyAliases.example: Compré flores ___ mi madre. / Pagué diez dólares ___ las flores.

para-deadline.example: Necesito el informe ___ el lunes. (by Monday)

para-viewpoint.rule: Para mí introduces a personal viewpoint
para-viewpoint.example: ___ mí, es muy difícil. (in my opinion)

para-employer.rule: Para can identify an employer or client

para-standard.rule: Para can establish an unexpected comparison standard

arrow-mnemonic.rule: The arrow and cycle are memory cues, not exhaustive definitions
arrow-mnemonic.example: What do the forward-arrow and exchange-cycle memory hooks suggest for the two Spanish for-prepositions?
arrow-mnemonic.answer: Para points toward a purpose, destination, deadline or recipient; por evokes cause, exchange, means or movement through.

gerund-endings.rule: Regular gerunds replace -ar with -ando and -er/-ir with -iendo
gerund-endings.example: Which gerund endings replace the infinitive endings of hablar, comer and vivir?

gerund-durmiendo.rule: Dormir changes o to u in its gerund

gerund-pidiendo.rule: Pedir changes e to i in its gerund

gerund-poder-exception.rule: Pudiendo is an -er exception to the illustrated -ir stem-change group
gerund-poder-exception.example: Why should pudiendo not be described as the gerund of an -ir verb?
gerund-poder-exception.answer: Its infinitive is poder, an -er verb with an exceptional o→u gerund.

past-progressive.rule: Progressive = estar (any tense) + gerundio (-ando/-iendo). Gerund is invariable.

legacyAliases.rule: Progressive = estar (any tense) + gerundio (-ando/-iendo). Gerund is invariable.
legacyAliases.example: Ellos ___ (estar, imperfect) ___ (hablar, gerund) cuando llegué.

gerund-invariability.rule: Only the auxiliary changes for tense and person in estar + gerund
gerund-invariability.example: In estoy comiendo and estaban comiendo, does the second word agree with the subject?
gerund-invariability.answer: No. The gerund is invariable; estar carries tense and person.

continuing-action.rule: Seguir or continuar + gerund expresses continuation

duration-llevar.rule: Llevar + duration + gerund expresses how long an action has continued

infinitive-after-preposition.rule: The taught antes de construction takes an infinitive, not a gerund
infinitive-after-preposition.example: Antes de ___, lávate las manos. (before eating)

future-plan-choice.rule: An ordinary future travel plan uses present or ir a rather than copying English progressive
future-plan-choice.example: How would you naturally announce Tomorrow I'm going to Madrid without copying English -ing?
future-plan-choice.answer: Mañana voy a Madrid. / Mañana voy a ir a Madrid.

infinitive-as-noun.rule: Use an infinitive for the activity liked in me gusta + activity

legacyAliases.rule: Spanish gerund is ONLY verbal (-ndo). For noun/after preposition → use infinitive instead
legacyAliases.example: Me gusta ___ (run) por las mañanas.

habitual-present.rule: The simple present naturally expresses a habitual activity
habitual-present.example: Give a natural Spanish sentence for the habit I study Spanish every day, without forcing a progressive.

relative-que.rule: Invariable relative que can describe a person or thing

bare-que-preposition.rule: Bare que after a short preposition depends on the construction
bare-que-preposition.example: Does La ciudad en que nací imply that every short preposition always permits bare que?
bare-que-preposition.answer: No. Bare que is possible in certain constructions; article-bearing forms such as en la que are also available.

relative-quienes.rule: Quien/quienes refer to people and agree in number
relative-quienes.example: Los estudiantes a ___ enseño son amables. (use the quien series)

restrictive-person.rule: A plain restrictive human relative normally uses que, not bare quien
restrictive-person.example: Why is El chico que vi the taught choice rather than El chico quien vi?
restrictive-person.answer: Without a preposition, this restrictive clause uses que; quien is mainly used after prepositions or in parenthetical clauses.

cual-agreement.rule: El cual/la cual agree with the noun they refer to in gender and number
cual-agreement.example: La razón por ___ cual vine es importante.

cuyo-possessed-agreement.rule: Cuyo agrees with the possessed noun, not the possessor
cuyo-possessed-agreement.example: El hombre ___ casa vendí vive aquí. (whose)

cuyas-novelas.rule: A feminine plural possessed noun requires cuyas
cuyas-novelas.example: La autora ___ novelas leo es famosa. (whose)

cuyo-register.rule: Cuyo is especially characteristic of formal or written Spanish
cuyo-register.example: Why might a speaker recast a sentence with cuyo in ordinary conversation?
cuyo-register.answer: Cuyo is relatively formal/written; a recast with de can express the same ownership more conversationally.

nominal-lo-que.rule: Lo que / lo cual refer to entire ideas, not individual nouns

propositional-lo-cual.rule: Lo cual can refer back to an entire preceding proposition
propositional-lo-cual.example: Llegó tarde, lo ___ me molestó. (which bothered me)

passive-structure.rule: A ser passive uses conjugated ser to mark tense
passive-structure.example: Which element carries tense in La carta fue escrita por Ana?
passive-structure.answer: Fue, the conjugated form of ser.

passive-agent.rule: Por introduces an expressed agent in the taught ser passive

passive-agreement.rule: In formal passive, the past participle agrees with the subject in gender and number
passive-agreement.example: Las cartas fueron ___ por el director. (escribir)

irregular-abrir.rule: Abrir has the irregular participle abierto

irregular-romper.rule: Romper has the irregular participle roto

se-agreement.rule: Se passive verb agrees in number with the grammatical subject (the thing being done)
se-agreement.example: Se ___ libros en esa tienda. (vender, present)

legacyAliases.rule: Se passive verb agrees in number with the grammatical subject (the thing being done)
legacyAliases.example: ___ venden libros en esa tienda.

se-singular.rule: A singular passive subject takes a singular verb

impersonal-personal-a.rule: Impersonal se with an a-marked human object keeps a singular verb
impersonal-personal-a.example: Se ___ a los sospechosos ayer. (detener, preterite)

human-passive-scope.rule: Human reference alone does not determine passive versus impersonal se
human-passive-scope.example: Why can Se necesitan médicos have a plural verb, unlike Se busca a los culpables?
human-passive-scope.answer: Médicos is an indefinite passive subject; a los culpables is a personal-a object in an impersonal construction.

passive-register.rule: Ser passives often suit formal writing; se passives and active clauses are common conversational choices
passive-register.example: Which passive construction conveniently names an agent with por, and which normally leaves the agent unexpressed?
passive-register.answer: Ser + participle can name the agent with por; the ordinary se passive leaves it unexpressed.

diminutive-tone.rule: A diminutive can convey affection or soften tone rather than describe physical size
diminutive-tone.example: Does a diminutive always mean the referent is physically small?
diminutive-tone.answer: No. It can convey affection, warmth or a softened request as well as small size.

cafecito-formation.rule: Café commonly forms the diminutive cafecito
cafecito-formation.example: El café está rico. Voy a pedir un cafe___.

legacyAliases.rule: Add -cito/-cita (not -ito) after words ending in -n, -r, or stressed -e
legacyAliases.example: El café está rico. Voy a pedir un cafe___.

diminutive-variants.rule: Diminutive suffix variants depend on the word and region
diminutive-variants.example: Do amorcito and panecito establish one compulsory diminutive suffix for every n-, r- or e-final word?
diminutive-variants.answer: No. -cito and -ecito are common patterns whose distribution varies by word and region.

lexicalized-diminutive.rule: Some historical diminutives have independent lexical meanings
lexicalized-diminutive.example: Why should bolsillo be learned as a whole word instead of translated mechanically as little bag?
lexicalized-diminutive.answer: It is lexicalized with the meaning pocket.

ico-regional.rule: Regional diminutives in -ico/-ica coexist with other forms
ico-regional.example: Where does this lesson locate common -ico/-ica diminutives such as momentico?
ico-regional.answer: Costa Rica, Colombia, parts of Venezuela and Aragón in Spain.

augmentative-tone.rule: Augmentatives can convey admiration or disapproval as well as size
augmentative-tone.example: Does an augmentative necessarily praise its referent?
augmentative-tone.answer: No. It can express admiration, intensity, large size or a negative attitude, depending on the word and context.

adjective-diminutive.rule: Diminutives (-ito) can be added to adjectives and adverbs, not just nouns

legacyAliases.rule: Diminutives (-ito) can be added to adjectives and adverbs, not just nouns
legacyAliases.example: Espera un moment___.

miss-family.rule: 'Echar de menos' means to miss someone or something
miss-family.example: ___ de menos a mi familia cuando viajo.

feel-like-pattern.rule: 'Tener ganas de' + infinitive expresses feeling like doing something

haber-nosotros.rule: Nosotros pluperfect uses habíamos plus participle

haber-ellos.rule: Ellos pluperfect uses habían plus participle

pluperfect-hecho.rule: Hacer has hecho rather than hacido

pluperfect-formation.example: Cuando llegué, ella ya se ___ ido.

past-before-past.rule: The pluperfect places an action before a past reference point
past-before-past.example: In Cuando llegué, ella ya se había ido, which happened first: her leaving or my arrival?
past-before-past.answer: Her leaving happened before my arrival.

temporal-cues-not-triggers.rule: Temporal words are context cues, not automatic tense selectors
temporal-cues-not-triggers.example: Does ya on its own force the pluperfect?
temporal-cues-not-triggers.answer: No. The pluperfect needs a past reference point and an earlier event; ya simply reinforces already.

prior-action-application.rule: Use the pluperfect for an action that happened before another past action
prior-action-application.example: Cuando llegó el jefe, tú ya ___ comido. (haber; completed before his arrival)

legacyAliases.rule: Use the pluperfect for an action that happened before another past action
legacyAliases.example: ___ habías comido antes de que llegara el jefe.

perfect-hecho.rule: Hacer uses hecho in compound perfect tenses

perfect-formation.rule: Present perfect = he/has/ha/hemos/habéis/han + invariable past participle

legacyAliases.rule: Present perfect = he/has/ha/hemos/habéis/han + invariable past participle
legacyAliases.example: ¿Alguna vez ___ comido ceviche?

life-experience.rule: The perfect can ask about experience up to now without a finished past date
life-experience.example: What time frame does ¿Alguna vez has estado en Perú? ask about?
life-experience.answer: Experience at any time up to now, without naming a finished past occasion.

perfect-regional-choice.rule: Recent-past perfect versus preterite is a regional tendency, not a continental correctness rule
perfect-regional-choice.example: Are Hoy he comido and Hoy comí separated by a rule that one continent's form is incorrect on the other?
perfect-regional-choice.answer: No. The perfect is common in current time frames in much of central/northern Spain; many American varieties prefer preterite for completed events, with variation within both areas.

perfect-cue-scope.rule: Words like hoy and ya do not mechanically force the present perfect
perfect-cue-scope.example: Does hoy make a simple preterite sentence automatically wrong?
perfect-cue-scope.answer: No. Time words interact with regional usage and the speaker's view of the event.

haber-invariability.rule: In haber + participle, the participle is invariable — never add gender/number endings

aunque-mood.rule: Aunque mood reflects how the concession is presented
aunque-mood.example: How does Aunque está cansado differ from Aunque esté cansado in the examples?
aunque-mood.answer: Indicative presents his tiredness as an asserted fact; subjunctive can present it as hypothetical or set it aside as irrelevant.

sino-replacement.rule: Use 'sino' (not 'pero') after a negation to mean 'but rather'

sino-que-clause.rule: A replacement clause with a conjugated verb uses sino que

unless-subjunctive.rule: Conditional a menos que takes subjunctive
unless-subjunctive.example: No saldré a menos que ___ de llover. (parar)

legacyAliases.rule: 'a menos que' always requires the subjunctive
legacyAliases.example: No salgo ___ que pares de llover.

provided-subjunctive.rule: Conditional con tal de que takes subjunctive
provided-subjunctive.example: Puedes ir con tal de que ___. (terminar, tú)

despite-indicative.rule: A pesar de que does not automatically require subjunctive
despite-indicative.example: Why is indicative llueve valid in A pesar de que llueve, salimos?
despite-indicative.answer: The rain is presented as an asserted fact; a pesar de que permits indicative as well as context-dependent subjunctive.

plural-address.rule: Latin American plural address normally uses ustedes; much of mainland Spain distinguishes vosotros and ustedes
plural-address.example: How does ordinary plural address in Latin America differ from the usual mainland-Spain informal/formal distinction?
plural-address.answer: Latin America normally uses ustedes for both; much of mainland Spain uses informal vosotros and formal ustedes.

voseo-present.rule: The illustrated present voseo of hablar is hablás
voseo-present.example: Vos ___ español. (hablar; the voseo pattern shown here)

voseo-ser.rule: Ser has sos in the illustrated voseo pattern

seseo-application.rule: In Latin America, 'c' before e/i and 'z' are always pronounced like 's' (seseo)
seseo-application.example: La letra 'z' en 'zapato' suena igual que la ___ en 'sala'.

regional-pronunciation-status.rule: Seseo and distinción are both standard regional systems
regional-pronunciation-status.example: Is seseo an incorrect version of mainland-Spain distinción?
regional-pronunciation-status.answer: No. Both are standard within their regions.

yeismo-sound-variation.rule: Yeísmo is the ll/y merger, whose sound varies by region
yeismo-sound-variation.example: Does yeísmo require ll and y to sound exactly like English y in yes?
yeismo-sound-variation.answer: No. It means ll and y merge; their shared sound may be y-like or, in Río de la Plata varieties, sh/zh-like.

regional-recent-past.rule: Recent-past tense preferences vary within as well as between continents
regional-recent-past.example: What broad regional tendency is illustrated by Ya comí versus Ya he comido?
regional-recent-past.answer: Many American varieties favor preterite for a completed event; much of central/northern Spain favors perfect for a present-connected event.

coger-register.rule: The social meaning of coger depends on region
coger-register.example: Why should a learner check local usage before using coger to mean take?
coger-register.answer: It is neutral in Spain and some American regions but has a vulgar sexual sense in many others.

address-context.rule: Address choices depend on relationship and local custom as well as grammatical number
address-context.example: Can a country label alone determine the polite pronoun for every interaction?
address-context.answer: No. Relationship, setting, age and local usage also matter.

informal-tu.rule: Tú takes second-person singular verbs in ordinary tuteo

usted-agreement.rule: Usted addresses the listener but takes third-person singular agreement

voseo-tener.rule: The illustrated present-indicative voseo uses tenés without a stem diphthong

legacyAliases.rule: Voseo verbs stress the last syllable and drop the diphthong
legacyAliases.example: Vos ___ razón. (tener)

vosotros-endings.rule: Regular present vosotros endings distinguish three infinitive classes
vosotros-endings.example: Give the present vosotros forms of hablar, comer and vivir.

colombian-usted.rule: Usted can signal closeness in some Colombian communities
colombian-usted.example: Does usted necessarily create social distance between Colombian friends or relatives?
colombian-usted.answer: No. In some Colombian usage it can express warmth and closeness.

mexico-plural.rule: In Latin America, 'ustedes' covers BOTH formal and informal plural 'you'
mexico-plural.example: ¿___ quieren ir al cine? (addressing a group of friends in Mexico)

switch-register.rule: An invitation to tutear can establish a mutually comfortable change of register
switch-register.example: What social move does Podemos tutearnos propose?
switch-register.answer: A mutual switch to tú address.

mente-formation.rule: A regular -mente adverb uses the feminine singular adjective as its base

mente-accent.rule: A -mente adverb retains the adjective's written accent

coordinated-mente.rule: Coordinated -mente adverbs may leave the suffix only on the final member

legacyAliases.rule: When chaining two -mente adverbs, only the second keeps -mente
legacyAliases.example: Lo explicó lenta y ___.

muy-quality.rule: Use 'muy' before adjectives and adverbs; use 'mucho' after verbs or before nouns

mucho-verb.rule: Adverbial mucho can quantify a verb without agreement

muchos-noun.rule: Quantifier mucho agrees with its noun

no-pronoun-order.rule: No precedes preverbal object pronouns in a basic negative clause
no-pronoun-order.example: ___ lo sé. (I do not know it.)

ningun-apocope.rule: Ninguno shortens to ningún before a masculine singular noun

postverbal-negative.rule: With no preverbal negative word, a postverbal negative normally requires no before the verb

legacyAliases.rule: When a negative word follows the verb, 'no' must also precede the verb
legacyAliases.example: No conozco a ___.

negative-concord-meaning.rule: Multiple Spanish negative words can express one negation
negative-concord-meaning.example: Does No tengo nada mean that the two negatives cancel and I have something?
negative-concord-meaning.answer: No. It means I do not have anything; the negatives reinforce one negation.

preverbal-negative.rule: A negative word before the verb replaces 'no' — never use both in that position

legacyAliases.rule: A negative word before the verb replaces 'no' — never use both in that position
legacyAliases.example: ___ viene nadie los lunes.

negative-agreement-response.rule: Tampoco agrees with a negative statement
negative-agreement-response.example: — No me gusta el brócoli. — A mí ___.

tampoco-position.rule: Tampoco follows the same word-order contrast as other negative words
tampoco-position.example: Why do Tampoco me gusta and No me gusta tampoco differ in whether no appears?
tampoco-position.answer: Preverbal tampoco supplies negation itself; postverbal tampoco needs a preceding negative in the taught clause.

cion-application.rule: The taught -tion/-ción noun correspondence preserves a written accent and feminine gender

legacyAliases.rule: English -tion words become -cion in Spanish and are always feminine
legacyAliases.example: The nation — la ___.

dad-application.rule: Many English -ty nouns correspond to Spanish -dad nouns

oso-application.rule: Many English -ous adjectives correspond to Spanish -oso/-osa

ble-application.rule: Many English -ble adjectives have related Spanish -ble forms

ista-application.rule: Some English -ist words correspond to Spanish -ista

greek-ma-gender.rule: Common Greek-origin -ma nouns can be masculine despite final a
greek-ma-gender.example: Why are el problema and el sistema not reliable evidence for a rule that every a-final noun is feminine?
greek-ma-gender.answer: These common Greek-origin -ma nouns are masculine; final a alone does not determine gender.

legacyAliases.rule: 'exito' means success, not exit — a classic false friend
legacyAliases.example: La pelicula fue un gran ___.

cognate-limits.rule: Cognate spellings are useful hypotheses, not guaranteed meanings or genders
cognate-limits.example: What should you verify before trusting an English-looking Spanish word?
cognate-limits.answer: Its actual meaning, gender and Spanish spelling, including accent marks.

skill-infinitive.rule: Saber + infinitive expresses a learned skill

como-qualification.rule: Saber cómo is grammatical for manner or procedure
como-qualification.example: Is saber cómo + infinitive always an error?
como-qualification.answer: No. Saber + infinitive is the basic skill pattern; saber cómo can emphasize manner or procedure.

saber-yo.rule: The irregular present yo form of saber is sé with a tilde

personal-a.rule: Conocer takes personal a before a specific human direct object

place-familiarity.rule: Conocer expresses familiarity with a place
place-familiarity.example: Yo ___ Madrid. (know the city from experience)

facts-saber.rule: saber = facts/skills/how-to; conocer = be acquainted with (people/places/things)
facts-saber.example: ¿___ tú la respuesta? (the answer = a fact)

conocer-yo.rule: Conocer has conozco in present yo

finding-out.rule: In the preterite, 'supe' = found out / learned; 'conocí' = met for the first time
finding-out.example: Ayer ___ que estás casado. (I found out yesterday that you are married)

first-meeting.rule: Conocí commonly marks a first meeting in the taught past-event context
first-meeting.example: ___ a tu hermano en la fiesta. (I met him there for the first time)

background-knowing.rule: Imperfect sabía/conocía describe background knowledge or familiarity
background-knowing.example: What contrast does sabía versus supe usually convey in these examples?
background-knowing.answer: Sabía describes already knowing; supe highlights the moment of finding out.

request-direct-object.rule: The requested thing is a direct object of pedir in the taught request construction

present-pido.rule: Pedir changes e to i in present forms except nosotros/vosotros

question-information.rule: Preguntar asks for information and conjugates regularly as an -ar verb
question-information.example: Ella ___ dónde está el baño. (preguntar, present)

request-bill.rule: pedir = request a thing/action; preguntar = ask a question (request information)
request-bill.example: Voy a ___ al camarero la cuenta. (I'm going to ask the waiter for the check)

preguntar-por.rule: Preguntar por asks about or after someone
preguntar-por.example: Me preguntó ___ ti. (asked how you were)

request-test-limits.rule: The request substitution test is a memory aid, not a universal translation algorithm
request-test-limits.example: What distinction should the request memory aid help you recall, even though English can request information too?
request-test-limits.answer: Pedir asks for a thing, favor or action; preguntar asks a question seeking information.

preterite-pidio.rule: Pedir is e→i stem-changing: pido, pides, pide… and pidió/pidieron in the preterite
preterite-pidio.example: Ayer Juan ___ una pizza. (yesterday Juan ordered a pizza)

preterite-pidieron.rule: Third-person plural preterite of pedir has pid-

event-location.rule: Location of a thing → estar; location of an event → ser
event-location.example: El examen ___ en el aula 3. (The exam is in room 3)

takes-place-cue.rule: Takes place is a cue for event-location ser
takes-place-cue.example: How does the English cue takes place help choose the verb for La fiesta… en mi casa?
takes-place-cue.answer: If is means takes place, the subject is an event: use ser, not the estar used to locate things.

death-state.rule: Permanence does not determine ser versus estar
death-state.example: Why does Está muerto use estar even though death is permanent?
death-state.answer: Spanish treats being dead as a state or condition, not an identity.

taste-application.rule: With ser, 'bueno/malo/listo/aburrido/rico' describe identity/character; with estar, they describe a current state, appearance, or taste
taste-application.example: La paella ___ muy buena. (The paella tastes great)

listo-contrast.rule: Ser listo and estar listo express different meanings
listo-contrast.example: How does Es listo differ from Está listo?
listo-contrast.answer: Es listo means he is clever; Está listo means he is ready.

temporary-role.rule: Estar de introduces a temporary working role
temporary-role.example: Este verano está ___ camarero. (working as a waiter)

recent-past-pattern.rule: Conjugate acabar and leave the following action in the infinitive
recent-past-pattern.example: Which verb is conjugated in the Spanish construction for having just done something?
recent-past-pattern.answer: Acabar is conjugated, followed by de and an infinitive.

present-recent-action.rule: Present acabar de expresses an action completed just now
present-recent-action.example: Mi hermano ___ de llamar. (My brother just called)

legacyAliases.rule: acabar de + infinitivo expresses a very recent action: 'to have just done something'. Use only in the present (just now) or imperfect (had just then) — never in the preterite.
legacyAliases.example: Mi hermano ___ de llamar. (My brother just called)

present-vosotros.rule: Vosotros takes acabáis in the present
present-vosotros.example: Vosotros ___ de llegar. (You have just arrived; Spain, informal plural)

recent-versus-finished.rule: Simple preterite acabar de expresses completion rather than this recent-past reading
recent-versus-finished.example: How does Acabé de comer differ from Acabo de comer?
recent-versus-finished.answer: Acabé de comer means I finished eating; Acabo de comer means I have just eaten.

past-recent-action.rule: Imperfect acabar de anchors recent completion at a past moment
past-recent-action.example: ___ de llegar cuando sonó el teléfono. (I had just arrived.)

pronoun-before-auxiliary.rule: Pronouns with acabar de + infinitivo can go before 'acabar' or attached to the infinitive — both correct
pronoun-before-auxiliary.example: ___ acabo de comprar. (I just bought it [el libro])

pronoun-on-infinitive.rule: A pronoun may attach to the infinitive after acabar de
pronoun-on-infinitive.example: Rewrite Te acabo de llamar with the object attached to the infinitive.

carrying-time-cue.rule: Carrying time is a memory aid for accumulated duration
carrying-time-cue.example: What does the carrying-time image help remember about llevar with a gerund?
carrying-time-cue.answer: Llevar literally means to carry; figuratively it carries accumulated time spent doing an action that continues.

ongoing-duration.rule: llevar + tiempo + gerundio = have been doing X for [time]. Negative: llevar + tiempo + sin + infinitivo.
ongoing-duration.example: ___ tres horas estudiando. (I've been studying for three hours)

perfect-not-banned.rule: Llevar is an idiomatic duration choice, not a ban on perfect-progressive forms
perfect-not-banned.example: Does learning Llevo cinco años viviendo aquí make He estado viviendo aquí cinco años ungrammatical?
perfect-not-banned.answer: No. The perfect progressive can be grammatical; llevar clearly emphasizes accumulated ongoing duration.

duration-word-order.rule: Duration may precede or follow the gerund
duration-word-order.example: Must the duration come before leyendo in a llevar duration construction?
duration-word-order.answer: No. Llevo dos horas leyendo and Llevo leyendo dos horas are both possible.

negative-infinitive.rule: Sin takes an infinitive in the negative duration construction

negative-duration.rule: For 'haven't done X for [time]', use llevar + tiempo + sin + infinitive
negative-duration.example: ___ dos semanas sin hablar con él. (I haven't spoken to him in 2 weeks)

past-duration.rule: Imperfect llevar measures duration continuing at a past reference point
past-duration.example: ___ dos años viviendo en Madrid cuando lo conocí. (I had been living there.)

duration-question.rule: Cuánto tiempo asks for accumulated duration

duration-vosotros.rule: Vosotros uses lleváis for the duration question
duration-vosotros.example: ¿Cuántos años ___ viviendo aquí? (vosotros; Spain, informal plural)

ongoing-present.rule: Ongoing hace… que uses the present for an action continuing now
ongoing-present.example: Hace dos años que ___ español. (estudiar; I still study it.)

ongoing-knowing.rule: Hace + time + que + present = 'for [time]' (still ongoing) — equivalent to 'desde hace + time'
ongoing-knowing.example: Hace dos años ___ a Andrés. (I've known Andrés for 2 years)

desde-hace-equivalent.rule: Present plus desde hace expresses the same ongoing duration
desde-hace-equivalent.example: Rewrite Hace dos años que estudio español starting with Estudio español.
desde-hace-equivalent.answer: Estudio español desde hace dos años.

ago-preterite.rule: Hace with a completed preterite event measures time ago
ago-preterite.example: Hace una hora ___. (llegar; I arrived an hour ago.)

que-not-sole-test.rule: Que alone does not distinguish duration from time ago
que-not-sole-test.example: Can hace… que occur with a preterite event meaning time ago?
que-not-sole-test.answer: Yes. Que may appear there too; inspect the verb tense and context, not just que.

hace-duration.rule: Hace + time + present = 'for' (ongoing); Hace + time + preterite = 'ago' (one-time)
hace-duration.example: ___ dos años que vivo en Madrid. (I've been living in Madrid for 2 years)

for-versus-ago.rule: The activity tense distinguishes ongoing duration from a completed past event
for-versus-ago.example: How do Hace dos años que estudio and Hace dos años estudié differ?
for-versus-ago.answer: The first means I have been studying for two years and still do; the second places completed studying two years ago.

question-tense.rule: Present and preterite questions ask different kinds of how long
question-tense.example: Does ¿Cuánto tiempo hace que llegaste? ask about an ongoing arrival?
question-tense.answer: No. It asks how long ago you arrived; llegaste is preterite.

negative-time.rule: No before the present verb marks a duration without an action
negative-time.example: Hace dos meses que ___ lo veo. (I have not seen him.)

present-habit.rule: Soler is conjugated before an unchanged infinitive
present-habit.example: Yo ___ desayunar a las ocho. (I usually have breakfast.)

unstressed-stem.rule: Nosotros does not diphthongize the present stem

vosotros-habit.example: Vosotros ___ cenar tarde. (soler; Spain, informal plural)

restricted-not-absent.rule: Restricted usage does not mean every non-present/imperfect form is nonexistent
restricted-not-absent.example: Does soler's restricted usage mean suela and ha solido are impossible?
restricted-not-absent.answer: No. Those forms exist; present and imperfect indicative are the main everyday habit forms taught here.

past-habit.rule: Imperfect soler expresses a past habit
past-habit.example: De niño, ___ jugar en el parque. (As a kid, I used to play in the park)

legacyAliases.rule: soler + infinitivo: present = 'usually do'; imperfect = 'used to'. No preterite, future, or conditional.
legacyAliases.example: De niño, ___ jugar en el parque. (As a kid, I used to play in the park)

habit-emphasis.rule: Soler explicitly emphasizes regularity already possible with the plain present
habit-emphasis.example: What does Suelo estudiar add to neutral Estudio?
habit-emphasis.answer: It explicitly marks studying as what I usually do, a recurring habit.

negative-habit.rule: Negate soler with 'no' before the verb: 'no suelo / no solía + infinitivo'
negative-habit.example: ___ ___ ver la televisión por la mañana. (I don't usually watch TV in the morning)

returning-to-action-cue.rule: Returning to an activity is a memory aid for repetition
returning-to-action-cue.example: How does the literal return image explain volver with an infinitive?
returning-to-action-cue.answer: Volver means to return; returning to an action means doing it again. The bridge a is still required.

repeat-action.rule: Volver a plus an infinitive expresses doing an action again
repeat-action.example: Si suspendo, ___ ___ ___ el examen. (If I fail, I'll take the exam again — use volver a)

legacyAliases.rule: volver a + infinitivo = to do something again — the most idiomatic way to express 'again' in Spanish
legacyAliases.example: Si suspendo, ___ ___ ___ el examen. (If I fail, I'll take the exam again — use volver a)

present-stem.rule: Stressed present volver has ue but nosotros and vosotros retain o
present-stem.example: Ellos ___ a leer el libro. (volver; present)

preterite-repeat.rule: The preterite of volver has no o-to-ue change

irregular-participle.rule: Volver has the irregular participle vuelto

pronoun-placement.rule: The object can precede volver or attach to the infinitive
pronoun-placement.example: Rewrite Lo vuelvo a leer with the object attached to the infinitive.

negative-command.rule: A negative tú command uses vuelvas
negative-command.example: ¡No ___ a decir eso! (volver; Don't say that again!)

negative-future.rule: No volver a + infinitivo = to never do something again (emphatic negative)
negative-future.example: ___ ___ a llegar tarde a clase. (I won't ever arrive late to class again)

place-versus-action.rule: A place signals physical return; an infinitive signals repetition
place-versus-action.example: Why does Vuelvo a Madrid not mean doing something again?
place-versus-action.answer: Madrid is a place, so it means returning to Madrid; an infinitive after a would mark a repeated action.

abstract-adjective.rule: Lo + masculine singular adjective creates an abstract noun: 'the [adjective] thing'
abstract-adjective.example: ___ ___ es que estamos juntos. (The important thing is that we're together)

article-versus-object.rule: Abstract article lo and direct-object lo have different jobs
article-versus-object.example: How does lo function differently in Lo veo and Lo bueno es estudiar?
article-versus-object.answer: Lo veo uses an object pronoun, him or it; Lo bueno uses the neuter article to form the abstract good thing.

relative-what.rule: Lo que introduces a relative noun clause meaning what or the thing that
relative-what.example: No me gusta ___ ___ dijiste. (I don't like what you said)

legacyAliases.rule: Lo que = 'what' (as a noun clause); lo de = 'the thing about / matter of'
legacyAliases.example: No me gusta ___ ___ que dijiste. (I don't like what you said)

topic-contraction.rule: De plus el still contracts inside lo del
topic-contraction.example: No me hables de lo ___ trabajo. (the work matter; de + el)

activity-topic.rule: Lo de can introduce an infinitival activity as a conversational topic
activity-topic.example: What does lo de introduce in No me gusta lo de levantarme temprano?
